pairs.match: Prints the full path of the current working directory
wrong_matches: Lists files and directories in the current directory
Changes the current working directory
pairs.feedback_correct: Yes! pwd stands for Print Working Directory.
pairs.feedback_wrong: That's another terminal command — pwd only shows the path.

pairs.match: Lists all non-hidden files and directories in the current working directory
wrong_matches: Prints the full path of the current working directory
Displays the installed Git version
pairs.feedback_correct: Correct! ls shows the contents of your current location.
pairs.feedback_wrong: ls is for listing, not for showing paths or Git versions.

pairs.match: Changes the current directory to 'archive'
wrong_matches: Initializes a new Git repository named 'archive'
Shows the state of the working directory and staging area
pairs.feedback_correct: Right! cd moves you into the specified folder.
pairs.feedback_wrong: This is a navigation command, not a Git command or status checker.

pairs.match: Displays the installed Git version
wrong_matches: Initializes a new Git repository
Lists files and directories
pairs.feedback_correct: Exactly! It shows the version, e.g., 'git version 2.46.0'.
pairs.feedback_wrong: git --version doesn't list files or create a repo.

pairs.match: Creates a new Git repository in the directory 'mental-health-workspace'
wrong_matches: Shows the state of the working directory and staging area
Displays the installed Git version
pairs.feedback_correct: Yes! The command initializes a repo in the given folder.
pairs.feedback_wrong: This is a repository creation command, not status or version.

pairs.match: Displays the current state of the working directory and staging area
wrong_matches: Lists all non-hidden files
Changes the current working directory
pairs.feedback_correct: Correct! git status tells you what's modified, staged, or untracked.
pairs.feedback_wrong: git status doesn't list files like ls, nor change directory.

pairs.match: Intermediate area where changes are placed via git add before being committed
wrong_matches: Records a snapshot of the repository at a point in time
Restores a file from a previous commit
pairs.feedback_correct: Exactly! It's the preparation zone for the next commit.
pairs.feedback_wrong: The staging area holds changes before committing; it's not the commit itself.

pairs.match: Stages the file README.md to be included in the next commit
wrong_matches: Creates a new commit with the message 'README.md'
Unstages README.md while keeping changes
pairs.feedback_correct: Right! git add moves the file to the staging area.
pairs.feedback_wrong: This adds a file to the staging area, it doesn't commit or unstage.

pairs.match: Creates a new commit from staged changes with the given log message
wrong_matches: Stages all changes in the current directory
Unstages a file but keeps changes in working directory
pairs.feedback_correct: Correct! The -m flag supplies the commit message directly.
pairs.feedback_wrong: This command commits, not stage or unstage.

pairs.match: A recorded, immutable snapshot of the repository at a point in time
wrong_matches: A Git object that stores a file's compressed contents
A unique 40-character identifier
pairs.feedback_correct: Yes! A commit captures the entire project state and is immutable.
pairs.feedback_wrong: A commit is not the content blob nor the hash itself.

pairs.match: Unstages summary_statistics.csv while keeping modifications in the working directory
wrong_matches: Restores the file from the previous commit
Creates a new commit that reverts the file's changes
pairs.feedback_correct: Exactly! The --staged flag removes the file from the staging area.
pairs.feedback_wrong: This unstages, not restores an old version or creates a revert commit.

pairs.match: Shows the commit history in reverse chronological order
wrong_matches: Displays changes between two commits
Restores a file from a specific commit
pairs.feedback_correct: Yes! git log lists all past commits.
pairs.feedback_wrong: git log shows history, not diffs or file restoration.

pairs.match: Limits the log output to the 3 most recent commits
wrong_matches: Shows commits since a specific date
Displays details and diff of a specific commit
pairs.feedback_correct: Correct! The -n flag restricts the number of commits shown.
pairs.feedback_wrong: This limits by count, not by date or a single commit's details.

pairs.match: Displays only commits made on or after April 2, 2024
wrong_matches: Shows only commits before a given date
Restricts output to a specific file
pairs.feedback_correct: Right! --since filters by a start date.
pairs.feedback_wrong: This filter uses a start date, not an end date or file path.

pairs.match: Displays commits made before April 11, 2024 (exclusive)
wrong_matches: Shows commits after the given date
Limits the log to a specific number of commits
pairs.feedback_correct: Exactly! --until defines an exclusive end date for the log.
pairs.feedback_wrong: --until stops before the date, not after, and not by count.

pairs.match: Displays the metadata and diff for the commit identified by hash c27fa856
wrong_matches: Shows the difference between two commits
Lists the commit history
pairs.feedback_correct: Yes! git show inspects a single commit in detail.
pairs.feedback_wrong: git show is for one commit, not a comparison or the full history.

pairs.match: Shows unstaged changes in report.md compared to the last commit
wrong_matches: Shows staged changes that will be included in the next commit
Restores report.md from the previous commit
pairs.feedback_correct: Right! git diff without --staged compares working directory to last commit.
pairs.feedback_wrong: This shows unstaged differences, not staged or restoration.

pairs.match: Shows the changes in report.md that are staged and ready to be committed
wrong_matches: Shows unstaged changes in the working directory
Creates a revert commit for the file
pairs.feedback_correct: Correct! --staged compares the staging area to the last commit.
pairs.feedback_wrong: This shows staged changes, not unstaged or a revert.

pairs.match: Symbolic reference pointing to the current commit (usually the latest on the current branch)
wrong_matches: A unique identifier for a commit
The parent of the current commit
pairs.feedback_correct: Exactly! HEAD is a pointer to where you are in the commit timeline.
pairs.feedback_wrong: HEAD is a pointer, not a hash or specifically the parent.

pairs.match: Compares the parent of the current commit with the current commit
wrong_matches: Shows the differences for the most recent commit
Restores a file from two commits ago
pairs.feedback_correct: Yes! HEAD~1 is one commit before HEAD, so this shows the latest change.
pairs.feedback_wrong: This command compares two commits, not a single commit or file restore.

pairs.match: Creates a new commit that undoes the changes of the most recent commit
wrong_matches: Removes the most recent commit from history
Stages the inverse of the most recent commit without committing
pairs.feedback_correct: Right! git revert is a safe undo that preserves history.
pairs.feedback_wrong: git revert adds a new commit; it doesn't delete or only stage.

pairs.match: Reverts the most recent commit using the default revert message without opening an editor
wrong_matches: Reverts without creating a commit, leaving changes staged
Restores a file from the parent commit
pairs.feedback_correct: Yes! --no-edit suppresses the text editor and commits immediately.
pairs.feedback_wrong: --no-edit still commits; it's different from -n or checkout.

pairs.match: Reverts the most recent commit's changes and stages them, but does not commit
wrong_matches: Creates a new commit that undoes the changes
Shows the diff that would be reverted
pairs.feedback_correct: Correct! -n stands for --no-commit, so the changes are staged but not committed.
pairs.feedback_wrong: -n prevents the commit, so it only stages the revert.

pairs.match: Restores report.md from the parent commit into the working directory
wrong_matches: Restores report.md from the most recent commit
Unstages report.md while keeping changes
pairs.feedback_correct: Exactly! The command retrieves the file as it was one commit before HEAD.
pairs.feedback_wrong: The ~1 fetches the parent, not HEAD itself, and it's not an unstage operation.
